stories.title: Design Token System Implementation
stories.user_story: As a mobile app user, I want a consistent visual experience across all screens, so that the app feels polished and professional
acceptance_criteria: Given the app is launched, When any screen renders, Then typography follows the defined scale (heading 24/20/16pt bold, body 14pt regular, caption 12pt)
Given the app is launched, When any screen renders, Then spacing follows the 4pt grid system (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48px increments)
Given the user has system dark mode enabled, When the app launches, Then all screens render in dark mode with appropriate contrast ratios (≥4.5:1 for text)
Given a screen reader is active, When navigating any screen, Then all text elements are announced with correct semantic roles
stories.reasoning: Design tokens are the foundation for all UI work. 3 points: token definition + dark mode support + accessibility baseline. No API integration needed.

stories.title: Reusable Component Library
stories.user_story: As a mobile app user, I want interactive elements to behave consistently (buttons, inputs, cards), so that I can learn the app's patterns once and navigate confidently
acceptance_criteria: Given any button component, When rendered, Then it supports variants: primary (filled), secondary (outlined), ghost (text-only), danger (red), each with loading spinner state
Given any text input component, When the user enters invalid data, Then an inline error message appears below the field in red with an error icon
Given any toast notification, When triggered, Then it appears at the top of the screen, auto-dismisses after 3 seconds, and supports success/error/info variants
Given any interactive element, When rendered on any device, Then the touch target is at least 44x44pt per WCAG 2.1 AA
stories.reasoning: Component library is the most effort-intensive design system task. 5 points: multiple component types, each with variants, states, and accessibility. Depends on US-001 for tokens.

stories.title: Tab Bar Navigation Structure
stories.user_story: As a mobile app user, I want to navigate between main sections (Offers, History, Profile, Settings) via a bottom tab bar, so that I can quickly access any area of the app
acceptance_criteria: Given the app is loaded and user is authenticated, When the home screen renders, Then a bottom tab bar displays 4 tabs: Offers (feed icon), History (clock icon), Profile (person icon), Settings (gear icon)
Given the user taps a tab, When the tab changes, Then the active tab is visually highlighted and the corresponding screen loads within 1 second
Given the user is on a sub-screen within a tab, When they tap the same tab again, Then the navigation returns to the tab's root screen
Given a screen reader is active, When navigating the tab bar, Then each tab announces its label and selected state (e.g., 'Offers tab, selected')

architecture_kb_sections: kb-L0-lloyds-enterprise-architecture §3.1 (Native mobile — Swift iOS, Kotlin Android)

stories.reasoning: Tab navigation is the app's primary navigation pattern. 3 points: 4 tabs with independent navigation stacks + accessibility. Standard native pattern (UITabBarController/BottomNavigationView).

stories.title: Deep Link & Notification Tap Routing
stories.user_story: As a mobile app user, I want tapping a push notification to open the relevant offer directly, so that I can act on time-sensitive deals immediately
acceptance_criteria: Given the user receives a push notification for an offer, When they tap the notification, Then the app opens to the offer detail screen within the Offers tab
Given the app is not running, When the user taps a notification, Then the app launches, authenticates silently (if biometric enabled), and navigates to the offer
Given a deep link URL is opened (e.g., from a shared offer), When the app handles the link, Then it routes to the correct screen based on the URL path
Given an invalid or expired deep link, When the app attempts to route, Then the user sees 'This offer is no longer available' with a button to browse current offers
Given a screen reader is active, When a deep link navigates to an offer, Then the destination screen's title is announced and focus moves to the primary content
stories.reasoning: Deep linking is critical for notification-driven engagement (the platform's primary interaction model). 3 points: universal links setup + notification payload parsing + error handling for expired links.

stories.title: App Error & Loading States
stories.user_story: As a mobile app user, I want clear feedback when the app is loading or encounters an error, so that I understand what's happening and can take action
acceptance_criteria: Given any screen is fetching data, When the request is in progress, Then a skeleton loading state is displayed (not a blank screen or spinner alone)
Given a network request fails, When the error occurs, Then a contextual error message is shown with a 'Try again' button that retries the failed request
Given the device has no network connectivity, When the user opens the app, Then an offline banner appears at the top indicating 'No internet connection' with cached content shown where available
Given a critical app failure, When the app cannot recover, Then a full-screen error state is shown with 'Try again' and 'Contact support' options
Given a screen reader is active, When an error or loading state appears, Then the state change is announced via an accessibility live region
stories.reasoning: Error/loading states are reusable patterns consumed by all subsequent epics. 2 points: skeleton + error + offline patterns using existing components from US-002.

regression_summary.recommendation: Greenfield — no regression testing needed. All stories build new capabilities.
